summary: Green Island Light in Green Bay off Marinette, Wisconsin: lit in 1863 with a fourth-order lens, kept by the Drew family, a shell since the 1956 steel tower.

light.characteristic: fixed white (1863 light); flashing white every six seconds (1956 tower, per Pepper)

structures.note: Walls only. Fire and vandals (Pepper; USLHS).
Coast Guard steel skeleton light, about 65 feet, east of the old station.

access.note: The island is private property. LighthouseFriends notes that the remains must be seen from the water or the air.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (service rights to the 1956 tower)

events.note: Congress appropriated $6,000 for the light (LighthouseFriends)
Station built 1862-63: brick dwelling with wooden tower (Pepper)
First shown the night of 1 October 1863
Kerosene lamp explosion; lens and lantern room damaged (LighthouseFriends only)
Peshtigo fire smoke; light kept burning day and night; light hard to see on the water
Schooner George L. Newman aground on the shoals off the island on 8 October; crew stayed about a week
Samuel Drew transferred to Menominee Pierhead Light
Well deepened to 20 feet; two landing cribs placed (Lighthouse Board)
Winter ice wrecked shoreline structures; boathouse rebuilt (Pepper)
Winter ice destroyed boathouse and landing (Pepper)
Frank and George Drew commended for rescuing two men and two women; Frank commended for going to the rescue of 24 people in a disabled power boat
Frank and George Drew towed a disabled gasoline launch on 21 July
Oil lamp changed to incandescent oil vapor; 1,700 candlepower (Bulletin; Pepper)
Towed disabled yacht Vanity to Menominee

Keepers cut off from the mainland in December; walked across frozen bay to Marinette (LighthouseFriends)
Winter light: 70 candlepower flashing white in the lantern (Pepper)
Plane that failed over Green Bay landed on the island; passengers kept overnight (Bulletin)
Explosion in the lighthouse on 31 January; inspector blamed a defective gas stove; $1,000 damage (LighthouseFriends)
Acetylene lamp with sun valve; keepers withdrawn
Roen Steamship Company bought the island except the lighthouse reservation (Pepper)
Light moved to a 65-foot steel skeletal tower; 1863 light discontinued
65-foot steel skeleton light erected by the Coast Guard east of the old station
Roen bought the lighthouse reservation; Coast Guard keeps the right to service the new tower (Pepper)
Coast Guard cutter Frank Drew (WLM-557) commissioned at Marinette on 17 June (LighthouseFriends)
Owner announced plans for a proposed $90 million development (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: Pepper gives the 1863 tower as 48 feet to the ventilator ball (about 14.6 m). About 65 feet (19.8 m) is the 1956 steel tower, so the record appears to give the later tower's height for the 1863 tower.
Only part of the 1863 walls remains (LighthouseFriends); the USLHS record says 'Only Shell Remains'. The 1956 steel tower is a separate structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both 'gone' and 'standing' fit. The 1863 dwelling survives only as walls (LighthouseFriends; Pepper), and the 1956 steel tower is a separate structure that Pepper describes as standing and flashing.

notes_for_editor:
- Sources for 1863 to 1890 (construction, first keepers, the 1864 lamp explosion, the 1871 fire and wreck, the 1881 transfer) rest on LighthouseFriends and Terry Pepper, who both cite the Lighthouse Board's reports of that era. The corpus holds Lighthouse Board reports only from 1891, so these facts are not checked against the primary reports. The 1864 explosion comes from LighthouseFriends alone.
- The USCG Historian's archived page for this light could not be read (the Wayback capture returned binary data). The Wikipedia article was read for leads only and is not cited.
- Chronicling America searches (four) for the 1871 wreck, the 1928 landing and the 1930 explosion returned no relevant pages. The Daily Northwestern article of 18 October 1928, named by LighthouseFriends, was not read.
- Read by position: the 1914 Bulletin notice sits in two interleaved OCR columns; the date and names were read from column order. The 1912 Bulletin OCR spells George as 'Georga'; quoted as OCR'd. The Commissioner FY1921 printed page is not confirmed, so it is cited by scan page 667.
- Roster match: the USLHS place 'Green Island WI (ruins)' has coordinates 0,0, so it was matched by name, state and dates (established 1863, discontinued 1956), not by position. roster.py's position candidates (Cana, Chambers, Pilot) were rejected.
- Record disagreements left open in the story: focal height (record 24.4 m; LighthouseFriends and Pepper give 55 ft, about 16.8 m, for the 1863 light, and the record may describe the 1956 light); range (record 7.8 nm; Pepper gives 14 miles in 1863, 15 miles after 1917, 10 miles for the 1956 light); fuel (lard oil, LighthouseFriends; sperm oil, Pepper); tower shape (octagonal, USLHS; square, Pepper and LighthouseFriends); land seller (McBride, LighthouseFriends; Samuel Drew, Pepper); Frank's first-assistant year (1902, Pepper; 1903, roster and LighthouseFriends); Frank's birth order (seventh child, LighthouseFriends; first of five, Pepper); Loyd (1921, Pepper; 1922, Commissioner and LighthouseFriends); Vanity (Pepper puts a Vanity tow in 1920; the Commissioner gives 1921); the oil house (Pepper and LighthouseFriends say 1897; the Lighthouse Board's FY1896 report describes it as erected, not used in the story); the 1912-1913 rescue (Bulletin 1912; LighthouseFriends and Pepper 1913; 23 people per LighthouseFriends, 24 per Pepper).
- Status: the record says 'inactive'. Pepper (last revised 2007) describes the 1956 steel light as flashing, and the USLHS record says the 1863 light was discontinued in 1956. The Coast Guard Light List was not read. Confirm whether the 1956 light is active before the record's status is changed.
- Not linked as other_stations: George W. Drew at Chambers Island (1903-1909) and Edward H. Cornell at Pilot Island (1900-1909) appear in the USLHS rosters under the same archive slugs, but no source connects them to this station beyond the name, so they are not linked.
- Mary Drew: Pepper names her as assistant keeper in 1867; the roster and LighthouseFriends name Helen. Mary is not on the roster.
- Green Island, Ohio (Lake Erie) is a different light. The 1919 Bulletin and the 1920 Commissioner report name a William L. Gordon there. Not used.
- Life-Saving Service table (FY1905, scan p.429) lists 'Green Island, Wis' among places where vessels stranded in several years from 1896 to 1908; the per-year counts are column-read OCR and are not used in the story.
- The owners' 2011 development plan is reported by LighthouseFriends as a proposal. No later source on it was found.
- Atmosphere: each scene detail is attributed to LighthouseFriends, Pepper, the Bulletin or the Commissioner. The only general context is one sentence from the 1881 Instructions, marked as general.
- Access: LighthouseFriends names Roen Salvage Company as the island's owner; the island is treated as private and the remains as viewable from the water or air only.
- Fact-check 2026-10-28 (story edits): the 1871 fire passage now names Keeper Drew, not Frank, as one of the fire fighters, as LighthouseFriends does; the 1912 and 1913 rescue dates are shown as conflicting with the 1912 Bulletin notice; the Vanity tow is dated 1920 by Pepper; the 1928 plane passengers are sent to the Coast Guard station (Bulletin) or to Menominee by boat (LighthouseFriends); the Pilot Island first-assistant promotion is dated 1 April by Pepper (the roster gives 1900).
- Copyright: LighthouseFriends and Terry Pepper's site are copyrighted, so the story now paraphrases them with at most one short quotation from each. Public-domain quotations are kept (Light-House Board 1893, the 1881 Instructions, the Commissioner's reports, the Bulletin).
